problem: Lead-acid car batteries drain when lights are left on, requiring jump starts, and are heavy.
business_model: Hardware: drop-in battery sold directly (target ~$200) via planned crowdfunding

founders.name: Hunter Scott
founders.background_notes: Hardware specialist with over 10 years designing electronics and building hardware teams per YC page.

competitors.name: Lead-acid starter batteries (incumbent technology)
competitors.what: Group 35 lead-acid batteries, 3 to 4 year life, about 40 pounds, typically $120 to $180

technical_complexity.rationale: Hybrid supercapacitor plus LiFePO4 pack with monitoring circuitry that must start engines reliably across temperatures in a standard battery form factor; hardware, safety and manufacturing for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Supercapacitor and lithium parts were available off the shelf; the TechCrunch piece names no patents, so copying by battery makers looked feasible.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found in sources reached.

market_need_then: Jump-starts and heavy lead-acid batteries are common pain; TechCrunch (2015-08) said Ohm targeted performance-car owners first, with about a dozen units in private beta. Willingness to pay at about $200 versus $120 to $180 was untested.

branding.domain_note: Used getohm.com, a get- prefix domain (date unknown).

brand_strength.rationale: One TechCrunch launch piece; no brand, community or merch evidence found, and the name is shared with many products.

outcome_analysis: Ohm launched in Summer 2015 as a supercapacitor and lithium drop-in car battery priced near $200, with a planned crowdfunding campaign and a dozen beta units. The directory marks it Inactive and getohm.com returned 503, but the cause of the shutdown is not public, and no funding, crowdfunding result or post-mortem was found, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Directory Inactive; exit.type shutdown is inferred from status only, date and cause unknown. getohm.com returned 503 earlier. A search snippet said one directory shows last activity in 2020 (unverified). Two outcome/funding searches returned only unrelated battery companies; an Australian unsealed4x4 page and a Product Hunt listing both mention an 'Ohm' battery but are not confirmed to be this company, so not used. No funding found, so coverage none_found, not zero. Founders not named in the TechCrunch article; names come from the YC page record. The only dated competitor is the incumbent lead-acid battery.
